title: Protonating acetone
subtitle: Acid makes the carbonyl carbon a far better electrophile

reactants.caption: acetone + hydronium (Cl⁻ is a spectator)
reactants.learnerPrompt: Draw the protonation of acetone by H₃O⁺.
hintTiers: Where are acetone's most basic electrons? Which species has an acidic hydrogen?
A lone pair on the carbonyl oxygen makes a new O–H bond, and one O–H bond of H₃O⁺ breaks. Two arrows.
Arrow 1: a lone pair of the carbonyl oxygen to a hydrogen of H₃O⁺. Arrow 2: that O–H bond onto the oxygen of H₃O⁺, which becomes water.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: The oxygen of H₃O⁺ carries the positive charge: it is the acid, not a source of electrons. Start from acetone's oxygen.
Curved arrows start where the electrons are. Start at the carbonyl oxygen's lone pair and point it at the proton.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Good start: the lone pair makes a new bond to the hydrogen. But that hydrogen now has two bonds, four electrons, and it can hold only two. Which bond must break, and where do its electrons go?

oxocarbenium.caption: protonated acetone, the oxocarbenium form
oxocarbenium.learnerPrompt: Draw the resonance form that puts the positive charge on carbon. Move only π bonds and lone pairs.
hintTiers: The positive oxygen pulls electrons towards itself. Which electrons can move onto it?
One arrow: the C=O π bond moves onto oxygen, which becomes neutral.
One arrow: the C=O π bond onto the oxygen. The carbonyl carbon is left positive.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: The π pair moves towards the positive, electronegative oxygen, not onto carbon.
That removes the proton again and gives back acetone. Here, keep the proton and draw the other resonance form.
Water can add to this carbon: that is how a ketone hydrate forms. First draw the resonance form that shows why this carbon is now so electrophilic.

steps.explanationAfterStep: Oxygen now has three bonds and one lone pair, so it is positive. A protonated ketone is a strong acid (pKa about −7), so only a little is present at any moment, but that little reacts fast.

The oxocarbenium form, with every octet complete, is the major contributor. The carbocation form shows the carbon's real character: much more positive than in acetone itself, so even weak nucleophiles such as water and alcohols now add.

mechanismSummary: A lone pair on the carbonyl oxygen takes a proton from H₃O⁺. In the protonated ketone, an oxocarbenium ion, the C=O π bond can move onto oxygen: the resonance form with the positive charge on carbon shows why acid activates carbonyl groups towards weak nucleophiles.
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 8 (Acidity, basicity and pKa)
